Definition: properly, something cutting; hence, gravel (as grit); an arrow
BiblicalUsage: Gravel is grit under the teeth, and both verses use it for what is hard to bear. Jeremiah says his teeth are broken with gravel stones, and Proverbs says the bread of deceit is sweet at first but leaves the mouth filled with gravel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God lets us taste the gravel so we learn the difference between sweet lies and true bread.
